danger_error_definitions.note: Rough proxies counted per report (a report is counted once in danger_total). They are NOT used in the harm test.
danger_error_definitions.missed_alarm: gold action is CREATE_VERIFICATION or UPDATE_INCIDENT and the system's action is NO_ACTION
danger_error_definitions.wrong_close: the system's action is CLOSE_INCIDENT and its effect on the task table differs from the gold effect (not counted if already a missed alarm)
danger_error_definitions.priority_too_low: same action as gold (CREATE or UPDATE) but a numerically LOWER priority than gold (3 = most urgent)
danger_error_definitions.danger_total: missed_alarm + wrong_close + priority_too_low (the three never overlap)
danger_error_definitions.false_alarm: gold action is NO_ACTION or CLOSE_INCIDENT, the system CREATEs or UPDATEs, and the effect is not a no-op (a wasted trip; reported separately, not in danger_total)

heads.model: StandardScaler + LogisticRegression(C chosen per head, lbfgs, max_iter=500, tol=1e-3); three heads: action (4 classes), sensor (3), priority (3)
heads.c_selection: grouped 3-fold log-loss inside the training rows of that head only
heads.random_state: none is set, and no random seed is used anywhere in head training: the same data gives the same head (deterministic)
heads.seed_in_heads_config: heads_config.json contains seed 20261110; it is NOT used by head training (only the bootstrap sampling uses controls_config.json bootstrap_seed)
heads.outer_folds: 5 folds by family (GroupKFold, no shuffling) for dev A; held-out B is answered by heads trained on all of dev A
matched_across_precisions: the same 1400 reports in the same order (checked with case_ids.json), the same dev/held split
the same training reports for every head: dev A only (held-out B is never used for training)
the same outer folds (GroupKFold on the same family labels gives the same folds for every precision)
the same labels, the same C grid, the same pipeline (StandardScaler fitted on the training rows of each fit, then LogisticRegression)
the same prompt (P1) and the same vector type: last-token hidden state, L2-normalised, 2048 numbers
NOT matched on purpose: the vectors (they come from the shrunk model), and the C that each head picks inside its own training rows

offset.definition: delta = mean over the 1000 dev A reports of (Q vector - FP16 vector); the Q vectors of all reports are replaced by Q - delta
offset.dev_a_note: The dev A out-of-fold answers use the same delta (computed from ALL 1000 dev vectors, including the vectors of the test fold). It is label-free, but the test-fold vectors take part in it.
offset.held_b_note: Held-out B answers use a delta computed from dev A only.
offset.explained_definition: explained = 1 - mean||d - delta||^2 / mean||d||^2 with d = Q - FP16 per report: the share of the average squared vector change that one constant shift accounts for. It is NOT a share of errors repaired.

bootstrap_heads.seed_of_head_b: bootstrap_seed + 1000 + b, b = 0..K-1 (head_id boot_01 is b = 0)
bootstrap_heads.sampling: whole families of dev A are resampled with replacement (a family drawn twice appears twice); about 63-64% of the families are unique in each sample
bootstrap_heads.meaning: bootstrap training-sample variability of the head on the SAME FP16 vectors. It is not a pure random-seed noise floor and it must not be subtracted from the separate-heads disagreement to get a quantization effect.

how_the_two_percentages_are_formed.bootstrap_vs_reference: mean over the bootstrap heads of the share of held-out B reports whose task table differs between the bootstrap head and the full-data FP16 head (both on FP16 vectors)
how_the_two_percentages_are_formed.bootstrap_vs_bootstrap: the same share between two bootstrap heads, in consecutive pairs (head 1 vs 2, 3 vs 4, ...). Head vs head, so about twice the variability of head vs the full-data head.
how_the_two_percentages_are_formed.not_additive: Neither number can be subtracted from the separate-heads disagreement to get a quantization effect.
